Grid: 12-column grid, strong left alignment, wide left margin
Hierarchy: One dominant element (about 60% of the weight), one secondary, small details
Notes: Works with one type family in two or three sizes.

Hierarchy: Title, image, date and place read top to bottom
Notes: Good for formal events; avoid centring long text.

Grid: Full-bleed image with a text block on a calm area
Hierarchy: The image carries the mood; text sits where the image is quiet
Notes: Check contrast of text on the image where the text sits, not on the average.

Grid: Two columns, 5-8 mm gutter, 12-16 mm outer margin on A4
Notes: Body 9-11 pt on 12-14 pt leading; 45-75 characters per line.

Grid: Modular grid of 6 x 4 or 12 x 8 cells
Hierarchy: Image sizes come in whole numbers of modules

Grid: Single text block; inner margin smaller than outer, bottom margin largest
Notes: Pick the proportions once and reuse them.

Grid: Same grid on every slide, the headline in the same place
Hierarchy: One idea per slide; the last slide asks for the action
Notes: Keep the edge clear; the next slide peeks in on some apps.

Grid: Single column with a clear F or Z reading path
Hierarchy: What, when, where, how to act, in that order
Notes: Put the call to action where the eye ends.

Hierarchy: One message per slide as the title; support below
Notes: Body text no smaller than 18 pt when projected.

Grid: Panels from the dieline, each panel its own mini-layout
Hierarchy: The front panel carries brand and product; the back carries detail and legal
Notes: Get the dieline from the manufacturer; never redraw it.

Grid: Left-aligned stack with 3-4 lines of information
Ratio scale: 1.25 for text, 1.5 or more for display
Hierarchy: Three to five sizes in total
